Compute the Population Branch Statistics with block jackknife standard errors

Source: R/jackknife_nwise_pop_pbs.R
jackknife_nwise_pop_pbs.Rd

The function computes the genome-wide population branch statistics (PBS) for each combination of populations, together with its standard error estimated with a weighted block jackknife. The PBS is a measure of the genetic differentiation between one focal population and two reference populations.

Usage

jackknife_nwise_pop_pbs(
  .x,
  type = c("matrix", "tidy"),
  fst_method = c("Hudson", "Nei87", "WC84"),
  return_fst = FALSE,
  block_size,
  size_unit = c("snp", "cM", "bp")
)

Arguments

.x

a grouped gen_tibble object

type

type of object to return. One of "matrix" or "tidy". Default is "matrix". "matrix" returns a dataframe where each row is a quantity (estimate, jack_estimate, se, z and n_blocks), followed by columns for each population comparison. "tidy" returns a tidy tibble where each row is one population comparison.

fst_method

the method to use for calculating Fst, one of 'Hudson', 'Nei87', and 'WC84'. See pairwise_pop_fst() for details.

return_fst

a logical value indicating whether to return the Fst values

block_size

The size of the blocks to leave out.

size_unit

Either "snp", "cM" or "bp". If "snp", the block size is in number of SNPs. If "cM", the block size is in centiMorgans. If "bp", the block size is in base pairs.

Value

either a data frame with the following columns:

  • quantity: the quantity reported in the row, one of estimate (computed on all loci), jack_estimate (the bias corrected jackknife estimate), se (the jackknife standard error), z (jack_estimate/se), and n_blocks (the number of blocks used)

  • fst_a.b: the Fst value for population a and b, if return_fst is TRUE

  • pbs_a.b.c: the PBS value for population a given b & c (there will be multiple such columns covering all 3 way combinations of populations in the grouped gen_tibble object)

  • pbsn1_a.b.c: the normalised PBS value for population a given b & c or a tidy tibble with the following columns:

  • stat_name: the name of populations used in the pbs calculation (e.g. "pbs_pop1.pop2.pop3"). If return_fst is TRUE, stat_name will also include "fst" calculations in the same column (e.g. "fst_pop1.pop2").

  • estimate, jack_estimate, se, z, n_blocks: as described above

Details

The genome is divided into non-overlapping blocks, which never span more than one chromosome, and pairwise Fst (and thus PBS) is recomputed leaving out one block at a time. The standard error is computed with the weighted delete-m jackknife of Busing et al. (1999), where each block is weighted by the number of loci it contains. See jackknife_stats_generic() for details.

References

Busing FMTA, Meijer E, Van Der Leeden R (1999) Delete-m jackknife for unequal m. Statistics and Computing 9:3-8.

Examples

example_gt <- load_example_gt("grouped_gen_tbl")

# Calculate nwise pbs with blocks of 2 SNPs
example_gt %>%
  jackknife_nwise_pop_pbs(
    block_size = 2,
    size_unit = "snp"
  )
#> # A tibble: 5 × 7
#>   quantity      pbs_pop1.pop2.pop3 pbs_pop2.pop1.pop3 pbs_pop3.pop1.pop2
#>   <chr>                      <dbl>              <dbl>              <dbl>
#> 1 estimate                  0.0461            -0.0110             0.0110
#> 2 jack_estimate             0.0743            -0.0274            -0.0512
#> 3 se                        0.0436             0.139              0.284 
#> 4 z                         1.70              -0.197             -0.180 
#> 5 n_blocks                  3                  3                  3     
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: pbsn1_pop1.pop2.pop3 <dbl>, pbsn1_pop2.pop1.pop3 <dbl>,
#> #   pbsn1_pop3.pop1.pop2 <dbl>
